corrected_value.authors: Cassidy, S., Roche, B. & Hayes, S. C.
corrected_value.title: A relational frame training intervention to raise Intelligence Quotients: A pilot study.

decisions.quote:
Previous analyses have reported increases in verbal intelligence following relational 

skills training interventions, a finding which is replicated in the current analysis (Cassidy et 

al., 2011; 2016; Hayes & Stewart, 2016). The Verbal IQ rises reported in the current study 

(M=19.6 points) are similar to the 18 point increase reported in Cassidy et al. (2011) which 

used a small sample of 8- to 12-year old children.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. (1) Empirical retesting: the paper motivates its single-blind randomized controlled trial of SMART relational training as a replication addressing the non-blinded testers and absence of control groups in Cassidy et al. (2011, 2016) (pp. 12-13), and in the Discussion (p. 21) explicitly states that the increase in verbal intelligence reported by Cassidy et al. (2011) is replicated in the current analysis, directly comparing the current Verbal IQ gain (M = 19.6 points) to Cassidy et al.'s (2011) 18-point increase. (2) Identity: cited in text as Cassidy et al. (2011) and listed in the References (p. 30) as Cassidy, S., Roche, B. & Hayes, S. C. (2011), 'A relational frame training intervention to raise Intelligence Quotients: A pilot study', The Psychological Record, 61, 173-198, DOI 10.1007/BF03395755 (confirmed in Crossref metadata). (3) Absence and non-equivalence: the only shipped row is input_row_index 20, Cassidy et al. (2016) (DOI 10.1016/j.lindif.2016.03.001, matched to sibling target 1). Primary text on pp. 8-10 confirms that Cassidy et al. (2011) (two studies of n = 8 children aged 8-12 and n = 8 children aged 11-12 using an earlier 5-stage/abbreviated WISC protocol) and Cassidy et al. (2016) (two experiments of n = 15 children aged 11-12 on WISC-IV and n = 30 students aged 15-17 on the DAT using the 55-level online SMART tool) are separate empirical studies with distinct samples rather than preliminary and full reports of one dataset. It is also distinct from sibling targets 2, 3, and 4.
